SPECIFICATIONS say
“On The Foundation On Button
Of Trench.
“In the ease of brick sewers
when the nature of the material
will permit, the trench shall be
trimmed for the reception of the
invert to the exact depth, ormand
size required. In case of any un
required variation in excess of
these, the space is to be refilled en
tirely to satisfaction of the engi
neer, and at the contractor’s ex
pense.”
The excavations for this work
on the gigantic “Enterprise”
called “Outfall Sewer,”looks as if
it had been done by a drove of
hogs turned in a potato patch.
And the filling In and so-called
tamping of dirt around the sewer
was done about as well as a
Shanghi rooster would scratch
around an ant bed.
It maketh the heart of the poor
taxpayer sick to look at this “Out
fall Sewer.”
CLEAN THE DIRT AWAY.
The specifications for the Out
fall sewer require that the contrac
tors shall clean the dirt away from
the open sewer for at least fifty
feet. But this has not been done.
An inspection of the Outfall sewer
shows a large embankment of dirt
piled up close to the edge of this
sewer. A heavy rain will cause
the dirt to wash and slide, and
till the sewer with mud. And the
poor tax payers will kick and say
“What’s the matter with our
sewers.”
THE MORTAR.
The specifications for the outfall
sewer say: “The volume of mor
tar shall be such as to fully fill
the void spaces in the stone or
gravel.” If you will examine this
sewer with a trowel, you will find
these “void spaces,” filled with
black dirt and sand, and a very
littlejcement. And then prepare to
“Cuss,” not Callaghan, but those
who are responsible for such shod
dy work.
BUILT A FISH POND.
The specifications for the outfall
sewer say: “No excavations for
earth will be allowed along the
line of the sewer.” But it was al
lowed, for near the beautifully
elevated plat of ground laid out
for the strawberry patch, (where a
little grubbing was done) close be
side the sewer can be seen a line
little lake dug out, about thirty
feet square, now filled with water.
The committee that received this
work, the Outfall sewer, must sure
ly have overlooked the special re
quirements laid down in the speci
fications.
CONTRACT! IRS 11ESP( )NSI BLE.
The specifications for the outfall
sewer say: “it is fully
understood that the inspection of
the work shall not relieve the
(contractors) of any of the obliga
tion to do sound and reliable work
as herein prescribed, and that any
omission to disapprove of any of
the work by the engineer at the
time of a monthly or other
estimate SHALL NOT be con
strued to be an acceptance of any
defective work.”
If you will pay a visit to this
outfall sewer, you will be
thoroughly convinced that Mayor
Callaghan is correct in the protest
he is making against thiscadly
constructed job.
EVERY TANPAYER
Who is interested in the welfare
of the city, and is asking “what
has become of all the money” we
are paying into the city treasury,
can find part of this question as
sured by pay ing a visit to the Out
fall sewer, and he will be ready to
at once proceed to “Cuss” at the
imbecility and rottenness dis
played there.
LET IT BE UNANIMOUS.
The city council should extend a
unanimous invitation to the
grana jury to pay a visit to the
Outfall sewer. They’ might do a
little wholesome investigation
that would open the eyes of the
community, as to how the public
money is squandered on botch con
tract work.
THE EMERGENCY MET.
When the ox is in the ditch its
no time to stop and discuss par
liamentary ethics; the thing to do
Is to go to work and pull the ox
out of the the mire. Thecity bud-
get was stalled, and while City
Dads Johnson and Hicks were
figuring on parliamentary tactics.
Mayor Callaghan with six faithful
props, pulled the city’ out of the
slough of despondency, ready for
business.. Now, let’s talk about
building at market house.

The forecast—Fair tonight and
Friday.
Weather conditions Slightly
cooler weather prevails throughout
the lower Mississippi valley and
southwest Texas, except on the
gulf coast where the temperature
is slightly higher.
Slightly’ warmer weather is re
ported from stations in the middle
west and in the central valleys.
No rain fell in the west or south
west during the past 24 hours.

THEIR INITIAL BALL.
The Ivy’ social dub will hold its
regular semi-monthly’ meeting in
Mission garden hall tonight, at
which the various committees
will report the progress made for
the club’s opening ball, to take
place Saturday night, October 16.
All arrangements are about
complete for the affair and the
committees will spare no pains to
make it one of the leading social
functions of the season.
FINED TEN DOLLARS.
Mr. Ed Braden -was fined $lO by’
the recorder this morning on the
charge of failing to put a street in
good repair after excavating for a
drain. The case against Mr. A. 11.
Shafer was dismissed.
POISONING OF DOGS.
A wholesale poisoning of watch
dogs has been going on in the
neighborhood of Chestnut and
Hays streets the past few nights.
The owners of these dogs are very’
indignant, as some of them are
fine animals. This morning no
less than six dogs which wore
poisoned, were taken away by the
trash cart.
(UMM LSSIONERS’ COURT.
The county commissioners this
morning awarded the contract for
lignite coal to the Carr Coal com
pany at $1.55 per ton The con
tract for McAlester lump coal was
awarded to John C. Mehan at $5 49
per ton.
The court appointed C. J. Gil
lespie, Esq to assist the county
attorney’ in the Deats-Elk horn
road case in the Thirty-seventh
district court.
The commissioners visited the
county jail this morning to inspect
the connections for the water sup
ply from the courthouse artesian
well, and pronounced it very satis
factory.
NEEDS ATTENTION BAD
South Alamo street, from the
corner of Commerce street to
Beethoven hall, is in a wretched
condition, and needs the attention
of the s’reet commissioner. The
street improvement committee
should take a look at it, and ren
der Mr. Mieklejohn the necessary
assistance.
BAPTIST SOCIAL.
The young people of the Sunset
Baptist church held a social last
night at the residence of Mr. and
Mrs. Sam York, which was attend
ed by Dr. Robert and wife, Mrs.
Wadkins, Misses Laura White,
Janie Ripley, Ella Lindsay, Han
nah and Mina Muenster, May
Brown, Alma Walters, Nora Orvis
and Messrs. Jas. Lindsay, Will
Walt -n, C. Robinson, James Perk
ins and others.
THE WEATHER.
Western Texas: Fair tonight and
Friday with southeasterly to westerly
winds.
WILL HAVE TO QUIT.
Madrid, Oct. 7 —lt is semi-officiaily
announced today that Captain General
Weyler will be recalled from Cuba this
month and that the cortes will be dis
solved in November and a new parlia
ment convened in March.
